sentences.text: This dinosaur is distinguished by very tall neural spines, particularly over the hips, with club-shaped tips on the first few tail vertebrae that may indicate old age.
A 2011 measurement of a 1.4-meter tibia suggests Barsboldia may have reached a total body length of 12 to 14 meters.
A Polish-Mongolian expedition discovered the fossil remains of Barsboldia in 1970 near the Nemegt locality.
The genus name honors Mongolian paleontologist Rinchen Barsbold, and the species name honors technician Wojciech Siciński.
Barsboldia fossils were discovered in Mongolia, representing one of the first hadrosaurid specimens found in Asia.
As a hadrosaurid, Barsboldia was a large bipedal or quadrupedal herbivore with hundreds of continually-replaced teeth adapted for a grinding motion.
If Barsboldia was a lambeosaurine, it would have possessed a hollow crest used for visual and auditory identification.
Maryańska and Osmólska originally classified Barsboldia as a lambeosaurine, the first such dinosaur described from the Nemegt Formation, despite the absence of a skull.
Maryańska and Osmólska described Barsboldia as the first lambeosaurine, or hollow-crested duckbill, from the Nemegt Formation, although it lacked a skull.
A 2011 study suggests that Barsboldia is indeed a valid genus of saurolophine.
Barsboldia is classified within the parent group Saurolophinae.
Barsboldia lived during the Maastrichtian stage, from 72.2 to 66 million years ago.
Due to the lack of a skull and only one partial skeleton, the validity and placement of Barsboldia have been debated, with some considering it a dubious genus.
A 2011 study suggests that Barsboldia is a valid saurolophine rather than a lambeosaurine.
